activity.title: 🥈I placed 2nd at the Divergent Teams national hackathon! After taking 1st at regionals back in May, I got an invite to compete nationally in Seattle. 2 weeks prior, an email came announcing it was an open competition, no tracks or themes and that we were free to start building right away. For the first week, half my time, I just brainstormed, trying to land on the right idea. Countless nights of research, following trails that led to nothing. I kept asking myself one question, “What's a huge, scalable problem that nobody's actually building for?” That’s how Neera was born. It utilizes sound detection sensors and satellite imagery working together to help towns find where underground water pipes are leaking. The final week was just building, teaching myself wires and hardware from scratch, alongside building a web app that connects to it. The 2-day competition arrived. I walked into a room with 20+ teams from all across the US and even India. I looked around and realized every single team had up to 4 people. I was the only one going solo. It should have felt like a disadvantage. Instead, it just felt like motivation. Day 1, finalizing and submitting: I was nowhere near where I needed to be. My hardware was half-working. My web app had exactly one page. Although behind and stressed, one quote kept me going. "You have a right to your work, but never to the results it brings." — Bhagavad Gita, 2:47 So I stopped stressing about the outcome and just kept building. Day 2, presentation day: Each team went to a private room and presented to a panel of judges. Only 6 were chosen to present again, live in front of the entire crowd and all the judges. Neera made that cut. After presenting to the whole crowd, it was time for results. Neera placed 2nd nationally, solo, against all odds and received funding to continue my journey. I want to also give a special thanks to Badari Ambatti for hosting, Divergent Teams , the judges, and James P. for the great advice! This is just the beginning more updates soon! 🚀 #hackathon #national #water #Neera #innovation #AI #WaterTech ...more

During YC Startup School, I played table tennis with Cory Levy . Honestly, I think the event that he organized called "Rising Frosh" was probably one of the best YC Startup School events I went to. I had the chance to talk to Grace Kasten and Cory Levy about what I'm currently doing and building during my time floating between SF, Boston, and Atlanta. Arhan Barve and I also had the chance to talk to Cory about some of the innovations that are happening at Laplace College Consulting (announcements coming soon!). DM me "College" for a free consultation btw. For anyone looking for a high-impact group of incoming freshman or even ambitious people in general, you can find SO MANY by signing up for Rising Frosh events (link in comments). For those who were wondering who won the table tennis match, I lost 11-6 to Cory, but he's like really good ykwim :) I'm also creating my own community of high-impact incoming freshman and college students. DM me "Incoming" to join our community to discuss building, get free housing whenever you need it, find hackathon partners, find co-founders, get free API credits, etc. 📷: Arhan Barve and I with Cory Levy at the Rising Frosh event in the Slash office.

For those just joining, here's Angel. Angel is a software system built for senior living homes, and this project means a lot to me and my team. But today's post isn't just about Angel. It's about a new experience. We were on a podcast. Professor Kev's podcast for young entrepreneurs welcomed me and my team so warmly, and honestly, nothing could have prepared me for how that experience would feel. I had never been on a podcast before and never thought I would be on one. And yet there we were, talking about our journey, our vision, and the work we're building together. The feeling was purely magical. To Professor Kev, thank you from the bottom of my heart. This was a absolute privilege. If you want to support young entrepreneurs like us, check out Professor Kev's other videos on YouTube and connect with him on LinkedIn!" If anyone wants to see the podcast, here's the link: https://lnkd.in/eS-9ZDmD The journey continues. 🚀 #YoungEntrepreneurs #Angel #SeniorLiving #Grateful #Podcast #StartupLife

Great story for you … We entered a pitch competition… Nearly 100 companies and founders were there, some founded by people from Harvard and MIT. Waited almost four hours to pitch and was never called. finalists had already been chosen... But my wife, coco ross , god bless her went backstage and demanded to give us a shot. They finally said yes. We pitched. The crowd went wild. They moved us into the finals. And we won the entire competition unanimously. That moment felt like the last four years of building our company. We’ve constantly been dismissed, underestimated and overlooked. Some people see Drew and assume we’re a cute school project led by a disabled kid. They don’t see the full picture. Over half a million followers. More than 2 billion views. Millions in revenue. Hundreds of thousands of dollars donated to help people with disabilities. For years, I thought we needed the people at the top to believe in us. I was wrong. We needed the community to believe in us. They vote with their follows, their shares and their dollars. That’s the lesson. You don’t need everyone’s approval to build something meaningful. You need a purpose people can rally around, the courage to keep showing up and a community willing to fight beside you. That’s all people with disabilities are asking for. Not sympathy. Not special treatment. Just a fair shot. Because sometimes the people who almost never get the opportunity are the ones most capable of winning it all. Happy and excited to continue busting down doors for the disabled community for the rest of my life.

Watching your child chase a dream with hard work, determination, and courage is one of the greatest joys a parent can experience. We are incredibly proud of our 15-year-old son, Aahish Abbani for earning 2nd place nationally at the Divergent Teams National Hackathon while competing completely on his own against outstanding teams from across the US and India. What makes us even prouder is not just the award, but his willingness to learn new skills, solve real-world problems, and never give up despite the challenges. His perseverance, curiosity, and passion for innovation inspire us every day. Congratulations, Aahish Abbani ! We are so proud of everything you've accomplished. This is only the beginning, and we can't wait to see where your journey takes you next. Keep dreaming big and making a difference. 🚀❤️ #ProudParents #STEM #FutureLeaders #Innovation #Education #Hackathon

At YC Startup School 2026, I posted a photo of Alexandr Wang ’s “top 10 mane.” Alexandr replied. Y Combinator reposted another post, and Garry Tan reposted another photo from the same afternoon. The throwaway jokes and ramblings reached 111.3k views. A couple months earlier, I spoke with Evil Rabbit , Vercel’s founding designer and former head of design, at Designers & Machines. I've met YC founders at my climbing gym, gotten hats and a JBL from VC partners, got sushi with a member of OpenAI. I met an OpenAI intern who once carried a briefcase with GPT-4o's parameters, and the friend of the owner of Molly Tea’s New York franchises explaining why they split from the China business. This keeps happening here. SF is so small that you keep running into the craziest people, and they can just as easily find you. The most memorable line from Startup School came from Alexandr: start from first principles. He built Scale AI after training-data friction blocked his own work. SF has a social version of that lesson. Put enough builders, designers, researchers, and founders into 49 square miles. Keep showing up. The people you follow become conversations. The conversations expose problems. Then the problems become things worth building. The talks were fantastic, but the city around them has been the real school 🌁
